summary: Cuba’s restoration pledges seek a 165,000 ha forest-area increase during 2019–2030, with 80,000 ha stated as achievable with domestic resources and the full 165,000 ha conditional on support; another formulation sets 50 kha unconditionally and 40 kha conditionally, including 50 kha during 2031–2035. The headline forest-cover goal is 33% by 2030. Conservation combines management of 75 kha unconditionally and 90 kha conditionally to reduce degradation, including 75 kha during 2031–2035, alongside forest-carbon uptake and removal estimates. The 165,000 ha expansion is about 3.8% of supplied 2022 forest area (43,115 km²), while the 33% goal is below the supplied 40.8% forest share. Agriculture targets 18,534 biodigesters, 5,000 solar pumping systems, full treatment of pig-sector wastewater, and lower dairy emissions through diet, manure management and silvopastoral systems. These livestock measures address a landscape where agriculture occupies 49.4% of the country; pig-sector emissions reduction is 8 MtCO2eq for 2020–2030.
